text: PPL / CAX / CFI (II-D) 19 sharp corners at the trailing edge of an obstruction. Air tends to naturally assume an airflow pattern where the air flows cleanly off the trailing edge. As the plate moves through the air, the air is unable to turn the corner at the trailing edge rapidly enough, and so the rear stagnation point eventually moves to the trailing edge. This is called the Kutta Condition: m See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutta_condition o When the Kutta Condition has developed around a flat plate, we can now see that a net circulation has developed, where air is moving more around the upper surface than the lower surface: © Itis also possible to see now that, because of this circulation, the air moving over the upper surface is temporarily accelerated compared to air along the lower surface, as well as redirected slightly downwards. In fact, the air traveling beneath the surface will never catch the air traveling above the surface. Because of this downward turning and acceleration of the airflow, downward momentum has been permanently transferred to the air. o Asa general statement, it is perhaps simpler to say, creating lift requires creating circulation, and when circulation is present, the airflow above will always be accelerated relative to the airflow below. If the airflow above is not accelerated relative to the airflow below, no circulation exists and no lift is being produced. e Incorrect Theories o Equal Transit Time - https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/k-12/airplane/wrong1.html o Skipping Stone/Bullets Theory - https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/k-12/airplane/wrong2.html o Venturi Theory - https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/k-12/airplane/wrong3.html e Airfoils and Airflow (Technical Discussion) - https:/Awww.av8n.com/how/htm/airfoils.html e “Bernoulli vs. Newton” - https://www.grc.nasa.gov/WWW/K-12/airplane/bernnew.html Prepared by: Ryan Binns (ryancbinns.com/flying), February 2020
